newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BONDS EASIER, SEEN STEADY TO FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BONDS EASIER, SEEN STEADY TO FIRMER.

text.p: 1630/1330 GMT - Finnish bonds end easier after fair Friday
trade but yields off highs, and potential seen for steady to
stronger performance next week, dealers say. *DEM/FIM heads back
towards 3.01 after weakening through 3.02 triggered central bank
intervention, dealers say. Markka jitters seen continuing.
*FIM-06 yld pct 6.30 vs 6.28 *06 gap over Bund bps 47 vs 47
*FIM-04 yld pct 5.88 vs 5.87 *FIM-99 yld pct 3.81 vs 3.75
*Jun FRAs 3.15 pct vs 3.14 *March FRAs 3.97 pct vs 3.89
*SEK/FIM 0.6757 vs 0.6727 *ECU index 101.01 vs 100.58

Bonds ended easier on Friday but yields came off highs, and dealers said they saw potential for firming next week as U.S. treasuries had started slightly higher and Bunds showed signs of strengthening in late trade.
"When there's no economic data, the trend is for bonds to strengthen everywhere," one dealer said, referring to next week's sparse slate of economic indicators.
"With little economic data due next week, we will probably see rangebound trade with the 2006 yield staying around 6.30 (percent)," another said.
Short-end yields fell after rising on markka volatility,
dealers said.
The markka began to recover, with DEM/FIM heading back
towards 3.01 after a burst of heavy foreign selling had sent it
through 3.02 levels and prompted central bank intervention,
forex dealers said, adding that the markka remained volatile.
"The problem is that this is a very flow-driven market," one
dealer said. "We could see a (DEM/FIM) range of 2.98 to 3.02
next week."
